Open thread • Replies: 153 • Updated: 2026-10-01 14:41 UTC

OP

Brazil has just wired a public blockchain into the official plumbing of a top-10 world economy. CSD BR, authorized by the Central Bank, the CVM and SUSEP to register, hold and settle securities, now mirrors live ownership records onto the XRP Ledger. The depository sits on more than BRL 22 trillion in registered assets, roughly $4 trillion, and can clear millions of transactions in minutes. No other public chain is in the stack.

The first assets are investment-fund shares from BTG Pactual, Latin America’s largest investment bank, which runs about R$2.7 trillion in combined wealth and asset management. Those shares are tokenized as Multi-Purpose Tokens on XRPL and paired with Ripple custody. CSD BR stays the legal source of truth for registration, deposit and settlement. XRPL becomes a permissioned, near-real-time audit layer that authorized banks can check under existing KYC and AML rules; no new licenses, no change in investor process, and with freeze and clawback still under CSD BR control.
That is the first time a licensed central securities depository has recorded securities ownership on a public blockchain in live market conditions. Once the mirror holds, the plan is native issuance and trading among approved participants, starting with CRI and CRA; the real-estate and agribusiness receivables that now form more than R$600 billion of Brazil’s private fixed-income stock after a fivefold surge in securitization over a decade.
